articles.title: Sydney Sweeney: Amy Hunt says advert is barrier to girls in sport
articles.summary: British sprinter Amy Hunt says she is concerned about the controversial advert starring Sydney Sweeney being part of a "barrier" to girls' participation in sport.
articles.body:
British sprinter Amy Hunt says she is concerned about the controversial advert starring Sydney Sweeney being part of a "barrier" to girls' participation in sport.

The advert for a sports betting company features the American actress naked but covering parts of her body with various pieces of sporting equipment.

After running a season's best 22.10 seconds in the 200m final at the Ultimate Championship in Budapest on Sunday, Hunt said: "This is what women in sport look like."

Hunt, 24, is among several female athletes who have spoken out against the advert's messaging.

"When we're trying to provide role models for young people and young women in sport, we really want to show that it's about what your body can do, not so much what it looks like," Hunt told Good Morning Britain.

"When we see the stats of 64% of young girls dropping out of exercise and sport before they reach the age of 16, we don't need to place any kind of barrier whatsoever in their way in terms of providing the opportunity and the empowerment for them to still exercise, whatever that looks like - professional or kind of just going to do a Parkrun with your friends.

"So it's about empowering young girls and young women and young people to show that you really can just get out there, and you don't have to worry what you look like. You don't have to worry about what you're wearing."

Hunt has enjoyed a breakthrough season, winning four gold medals at the European Championships in Birmingham last month.

She said "sport is not pretty", describing how she is often sick during sessions or in tears if something does not go to plan.

Hunt said the responses to Sweeney's advert had eclipsed the controversy.

"The reaction has almost outweighed the moment because the first thing I saw was all of the positive compilations of women in sport," she said.

articles.title: World Athletics Championships 2029: Kenyan capital Nairobi wins bid to host event in African first
articles.summary: Kenya will become the first African nation to host the World Athletics Championships after Nairobi beats London, Munich and Rome in bidding for the 2029 event.
articles.body:
Kenya will become the first African country to host the World Athletics Championships after winning the bid for the 2029 edition.

The capital Nairobi will hold the event at the 48,000-capacity Kasarani Stadium.

London and Rome were the cities to miss out, with Munich awarded hosting rights in 2031.

Kenya's rich athletics heritage was central to its bid for 2029, with the East African nation boasting 72 World Championship and 38 Olympic gold medals, predominantly in middle- and long-distance running.

It is the second-most successful nation in the history of the World Championships, and two-time Olympic marathon champion Eliud Kipchoge, who also won 5000m gold at the 2003 World Championships, was among those who made the case for Nairobi during the bid process.

World Athletics president Sebastian Coe described that bid as "compelling and emotional".

"Kenya is one of the great athletics nations," Coe added.

"The sport is woven into the fabric of the country.

"It was important that the World Championships should come to Africa when we had the right host, the right bid and the right circumstances. Nairobi has demonstrated emphatically that this is their moment."

The decision to award the event to Nairobi is historic for Africa, with the continent having never hosted the senior World Championships despite producing some of the sport's biggest stars.

Kenya's bid also highlighted its experience of hosting major athletics events, including the 2017 World Under-18 and 2021 World U20 Championships in Nairobi and the 2007 World Cross Country Championships in Mombasa.

Kenya previously bid to stage the 2025 World Championships but lost out to Tokyo, with infrastructure a key weakness.

This time, the country pointed to upgrades to existing facilities as evidence of its readiness.

Kenya has been renovating its stadiums ahead of co-hosting next year's Africa Cup of Nations alongside Tanzania and Uganda.

Kasarani Stadium is undergoing a complete structural overhaul in the build-up to hosting games at the continent's biggest football tournament.

articles.title: Nairobi y Munich acogerán los próximos Mundiales en 2029 y 2031
articles.standfirst: Por primera vez África será sede de esta competición del atletismo
articles.summary: Será la primera vez que África acoja esta competición del atletismo
articles.body: Tras uno de los procesos de licitación más reñidos de la historia de esta competición, Nairobi y Múnich han sido seleccionadas para albergar los Campeonatos del Mundo de atletismo de 2029 y 2031, respectivamente. Esta decisión, que se adoptó durante la reunión de la Comisión de World Athletics, supone que el Mundial se celebrará en África por primera vez en 2029, antes de regresar a Alemania por tercera vez dos años después, esta vez en el emblemático Estadio Olímpico de Múnich. “No fue una decisión fácil para el Consejo”, declaró el presidente de World Athletics, Sebastian Coe. “La calidad, la ambición y el compromiso demostrados por los cuatro candidatos subrayan la fortaleza y el atractivo global del Mundial”. En este sentido, Coe hizo hincapié en que “con esta decisión del Consejo, seguimos cumpliendo nuestra misión de impulsar el atletismo a nivel mundial mediante la celebración de nuestros campeonatos en Asia, África y Europa durante sus próximas tres ediciones". La elección de Nairobi supone un hito dentro del atletismo, con la celebración de su mayor competición en el continente africano por primera vez. En los últimos años, World Athletics ya ha celebrado en África diferentes eventos. Por ejemplo, Kampala (Uganda) acogió el Mundial de cross en 2017; mientras Nairobi ha albergado los Mundiales sub18 y sub20 en distinas ediciones, eventos que han contribuido a acumular una valiosa experiencia y conocimientos en la organización de competiciones. Coe explicó que "Nairobi presentó una candidatura convincente y emotiva y llevar el Mundial a África por primera vez será histórico. Kenia es una de las grandes naciones del atletismo. Este deporte está arraigado en la cultura del país, y atletas como los medallistas de oro mundiales Kipyegon, Cheruiyot, Kipchoge, Obiri y Rudisha, entre otros, han marcado la historia de nuestro deporte".

articles.title: Hockey India mess 'not something that can't be resolved': Sports Ministry source
articles.summary: Hockey News: NEW DELHI: The Sports Ministry is positive of resolving the ongoing mess among warring factions in Hockey India. A source said they will, however, wai.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Sports Ministry is positive of resolving the ongoing mess among warring factions in Hockey India. A source said they will, however, wait for an amicable resolution internally before seeing the need to step in."Let them resolve it amicably, mutually. It is not an issue that can't be resolved. It is our responsibility to fix it. Like football, hockey needs to also work in similar manner with its league. Whether ministry intervention is needed would be decided once it is clear that the situation is not getting resolved," a Sports Ministry source said.Hockey India (HI) chief Dilip Tirkey, who is a former player, and the body's secretary general Bhola Nath Singh have been locked in a public tug of war ever since the decision to change the teams' jersey colour from blue to saffron ahead of the World Cup. The move was criticised outside the hockey circles.In the aftermath, Tirkey has said on the record that he was not consulted before the decision was made. He further issued a show cause notice last week to HI Director General, Cdr R K Srivastava, who is perceived to be close to Singh.Bhola Nath Singh, meanwhile, has called an Emergent Board Meeting (EGM) on September 18 to discuss the current situation.Tirkey, meanwhile, insisted that he has not approved any such meeting and would not do so until he receives a response from Srivastava on the jersey fiasco, among other issues.The Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya had met the Hockey India top brass, including Tirkey, on Monday where the Hockey India League's (HIL) roadmap and sustainability was discussed. Bhola Nath Singh and acting Director General Ranjit Gill joined the meeting virtually.Cdr R K Srivastava did attend an official event in Mohali alongside Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, Executive Board member R P Singh, as dates and venues of the 2026 men's Asian Champions Trophy were announced.India men's team had finished eighth at the FIH World Cup in Belgium and Netherlands and the women's had done better to finish fifth.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jake Paul's Fiancee Jutta Leerdam Shares New Video on Speedskating Future, 'Am I Retiring?'
articles.summary: Three-time Olympic medalist speed skater Jutta Leerdam of the Netherlands is sitting out next season but did not rule out a return to competition in the future.
articles.body:
Three-time Olympic medalist speed skater Jutta Leerdam of the Netherlands is sitting out next season but did not rule out a return to competition in the future.

Leerdam, who is engaged to boxer Jake Paul, shared the announcement in a Monday video on her YouTube channel.

"Am I retiring? One thing is for sure— you will not see me skate this season, that's for sure," Leerdam said around the 8:00 mark of the video. "I will not be competing this year, that's for sure, so you will not see me on the ice."

Leerdam added she is not ready to "fully close the door" on potentially returning to speed skating in the future.

"I'm 27. Life changes, feelings change, and I wouldn't feel comfortable saying I'm fully retiring forever," Leerdam said.

Leerdam and Paul shared the news of their engagement in 2025. Leerdam's latest announcement was shared seven months after she became an Olympic champion at the 2026 Milan Cortina Games.

She set an Olympic record and won her first Olympic gold medal with a time of 1:12.31 in the women's 1,000-meter speed skating final.

Leerdam also won silver in the women's 500m in February to mark the third Olympic medal of her career. She previously won silver in the women's 1,000m during the 2022 Beijing Olympics.

After winning her first global title during the 2017 World Junior Championships, Leerdam has won six world championship gold medals in her adult career.

Sitting out the season will sideline Leerdam for the world championships next February in Beijing. It remains to be seen if she will return to the ice in time for the 2030 Winter Olympics in the French Alps.

articles.title: IOA announces Randhir Singh, Jaspal Rana memorial trophies for best Asian Games athletes
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha on Tuesday announced two memorial awards named after veteran sports administrator late Randhir.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha on Tuesday announced two memorial awards named after veteran sports administrator late Randhir Singh and shooting great Jaspal Rana.The awards will be given to the best male and female athletes at the Asian Games.Singh served as the IOA secretary general for 25 years from 1987 to 2012. He also served as the president of the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA). Singh died at the age of 79 in May this year.Rana, a multiple Asian and Commonwealth Games medallist and renowned pistol coach, died at the age of 49 in June. He was the coach of double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker.Awards to honour Asian Games starsUsha made the announcement during the launch of a book on Rana titled "Maverick Jaspal", co-authored by senior sports journalists S Kannan and G Rajaraman."From this year, the IOA has decided to introduce two memorial trophies in the names of legendary Raja Randhir Singh and shooting great Jaspal Rana for the best athletes in the Asian Games," she said."The Raja Randhir Singh Trophy will be awarded to the best male athlete of the Asian Games, while the Jaspal Rana Trophy will be awarded to the best female athlete of the Asian Games to honour their contribution to Indian sports."Usha says no accommodation issues so farUsha also said there were no accommodation-related issues for the Indian contingent at Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, which is hosting the Asian Games.She said Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav would handle any problems if they arise."They (organisers) have to give rooms because they are the organisers. From our side, we will do our best, and there is a Chef de Mission, and if there are any problems, he will solve them," said Usha, who will leave for Japan on Wednesday.'We are Team India'Asked about accommodation-related problems for the Indian cricket teams, Usha said: "I didn't get any complaints from there. They are all athletes, and we are Team India."Usha does not want to put pressure on athletesThe IOA chief also said she did not want to put any pressure on the athletes competing at the Asian Games."I don't want to give any pressure to our athletes. I think they have all gone there with confidence. Hope that they will do their best. The Indian government, sports ministry, and IOA have already provided them with whatever they wanted."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
